data.narrative:
Andrenam is a Series A defense and security company founded by Matej Cernosek and Alex Chu that has raised $18M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Singularity.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the $18M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-round progression, implying $36M. Peer-median analysis across the 11-company comp set yields a $1.0B median valuation, with a range spanning $125M (low) to $3.0B (high). The peer distribution reflects heterogeneous outcomes in an early-stage, high-variance sector; representative Series B comparables include Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), and Harmattan AI ($1.4B).

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $31M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $518M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Andrenam's ability to reach peer-scale outcomes. Key variables include technology differentiation relative to the named peer set, addressable market capture assumptions, and path to Series B funding. The peer-median method dominates due to direct comparability; the stage-progression method serves primarily as a floor check.
